details: cat-sis2go-utils is an npm package whose only functional code is an install hook that beacons the installing machine to an attacker-controlled out-of-band collector. package.json declares preinstall and postinstall as "node scripts/run.js", so the hook runs unconditionally on every npm install of the package. scripts/run.js performs a DNS lookup of a unique subdomain under dnshook.site (a DNS canary service) and an HTTP POST to a hardcoded webhook.site endpoint (https://webhook.site/d22d92dc-84e5-4b58-8cd6-75bf1ac452c7). In 99.0.0 the POST carries the lifecycle phase and package identity; in 99.1.0 it additionally collects os.hostname() and os.userInfo().username and sends them in the POST body. The package.json description calls the package a dependency-confusion proof of concept, but it is published on the public registry under a name that mimics an internal package, executes at install time for anyone who resolves it, and exfiltrates host identity to a third-party collector with no consent, no documented feature and no opt-out. The webhook.site and dnshook.site hosts are shared services and are given as full URLs only, not as blockable domains. pkgwarden reviewed both versions from the published tarballs with two independent readers.
